title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rotary optimizations + KV batching
author: Alex Kim
description: Background: This PR upgrades the serving runtime's attention kernels to a consolidated FlashAttnV2 implementation, introduces fused rotary/rope ops, and adds KV-aware batching hooks to reduce redundant KV copies. Motivation: reduce per-token latency and memory pressure for long-context models and improve throughput under mixed workloads. Changes summary: replace legacy attention paths with flashattn_v2 kernels (CUDA/C++), add fused rotary application in the kernel pipeline to avoid extra tensor ops, introduce an opt-in KV batching path that coalesces KV cache updates across concurrent requests, tune scheduler heuristics to prefer KV-local batches, add new benchmarks and integration tests. Compatibility: runtime falls back to legacy kernels when FlashAttnV2 is not available; rollout gating via runtime config flags. Testing: microbenchmarks (latency/p99), end-to-end inference tests, CI perf job, and internal canary on dedicated fleet. Impact: expected 15-35% token throughput improvement on A100 for decoder-only models and 20-40% latency reduction for long-context (>= 8k) scenarios depending on workload. Rollout plan: feature flag, staged canary, monitoring dashboards, automatic rollback on perf regressions. Related: ENG-4216, ENG-4217, DOC-189.
commits: feat(attn): add flashattn_v2 kernels and C++ wrappers; perf(attn): fuse rotary/rope into attention kernel; feat(kv): introduce KV batching coalescer and scheduler hooks; refactor(scheduler): add kv_local_batch heuristic; test(bench): add bench_attn long context suites; ci: add perf job and canary pipeline; docs: perf notes and rollout checklist
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can we keep the legacy kernel compilation flag to allow customers without required CUDA kernels to keep serving? (answered: feature flag present; fallback implemented)

Priya Desai: The fused rotary op looks good but it changes numerical ordering; please add a unit test that asserts parity within epsilon over long contexts. (author reply: added test_kv_batcher parity checks and bench parity harness)
Marco Alvarez: Consider exposing telemetry metrics for KV coalescing rate to aid debugging in Dedicated fleets. (author reply: added kv.coalesce_rate counter and dashboard tile)
release_notes: Improved attention kernels: FlashAttnV2 backend with fused rotary/rope ops and KV batching for reduced latency and increased throughput. Opt-in via runtime.featureFlags.attn_flashattn_v2; fallback to legacy kernels when unavailable.
